subject: KiteWave integration: peering/gateway routing, egress & mTLS next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@kitewave.io>; Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@kitewave.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KiteWave integration: peering/gateway routing, egress & mTLS next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on product fit and the high-level deployment we recommended. Recap and concrete next steps below so we can move the tech validation forward.

Key decisions from the call:
- You want a private onramp: VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) to keep inference traffic off the public internet.
- Traffic routing: edge proxy in your account -> PrivateLink endpoint -> Redwood private fleet.
- Security: mutual TLS for the control plane + IP allowlist for token-restricted admin endpoints.
- Outputs: you will need structured tool-calling support (JSON schema output) and an embeddings/reranker flow for semantic search.

Immediate asks for your engineering team (what we need to validate):
1) Network details: prefer a single /28 for the PrivateLink endpoint? If not, send the CIDR(s) you can allocate and any security group constraints.
2) Egress policy: do your egress rules require DNS proxying (outbound via a corporate resolver) or can we use Redwood-managed resolvers?
3) mTLS: who will sign your client certificates (internal CA or cloud KMS/HSM)? If you have an existing rotated cert process, send the rotation window.
4) Embeddings volume: expected daily embedding batches (avg records/day) + typical vector dim if known (so we can size reranker/throughput).

Attachments: I attached our short patterns doc (redwood-egress-patterns.pdf) and a blank answers spreadsheet for the networking items.

Next steps / owners:
- Your engineering: fill the networking spreadsheet by EOD Fri (Sofia).
- Redwood SEs: Ben will schedule a 1-hour deep-dive for the PrivateLink design; I'll join for routing/auth details.
- Legal/Proc: we'll surface any data residency flags in the next contract iteration.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if easier.

--
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0138
[Attachment: redwood-egress-patterns.pdf (3 pages, PDF)]

From: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@kitewave.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@kitewave.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KiteWave integration: peering/gateway routing, egress & mTLS next steps

Diego — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from our side and a couple of clarifying Qs inline.

1) CIDR: We can carve out a /28 from our shared services VPC. Will confirm the exact block by EOD Thu (Sofia to provide).
2) Egress/DNS: We have a corporate DNS proxy that resolves outbound to internal names (logging + filtering). Ideally we'd keep DNS on our resolver; is there a way to explicitly point requests to it rather than Redwood-managed DNS? That was a blocker for another vendor.
3) mTLS: We use a cloud KMS to issue certs via our automation pipelines. Rotation is at 30 days. Fine with mTLS but need details on the client auth handshake (SNI usage, expected CN format).
4) Embeddings: initial pilot ~10k documents/day, vectors are 1536-d. Production target could be 200k/day in 2 quarters.

Also: Any constraints on Source IPs we should anticipate for the PrivateLink endpoint? We'll need to add allowlist rules on our egress ACLs.

I'll populate the spreadsheet with the current values and drop in the CIDR once confirmed.

On the DNS point — can Ben or Lauren confirm whether Redwood supports using a customer-supplied resolver for outbound lookups over the PrivateLink path?

Thanks,
Amir

--
Amir Qureshi
Head of Platform Engineering, KiteWave
amir.qureshi@kitewave.io | +1 (617) 555-2244

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@kitewave.io>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@kitewave.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 12:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KiteWave integration: peering/gateway routing, egress & mTLS next steps

Amir — great, appreciate the quick responses and the volume numbers — that'll help sizing. Short answers below and a few more details attached.

- DNS/resolver: yes, we can support a customer-provided resolver over the PrivateLink path. Implementation options: 1) Force all outbound lookups to your resolver by advertising a specific route and pushing the resolver IP into the proxy config, or 2) If you prefer, we can NAT DNS to your resolver via a small eBPF hook in the edge proxy. Option 1 is cleaner for auditing.

- Source IPs: PrivateLink endpoints will present a small set of stable ENIs in your VPC (we typically request a /28). We'll provide the specific IPs once the endpoint is provisioned; for planning assume 3-6 IPs for control/ingress/data planes.

- mTLS handshake: we support standard mutual TLS with client certs signed by your CA. Expected CN pattern is free-form but we recommend service/<team>-<env> as an identifier; SNI is not required for the control channel but is used for routing on the edge proxy for multi-tenant hostnames. Rotation at 30 days is fine — we support automated cert replacement via our cert-rotate webhook (we'll provide a small webhook spec).

Attached is a short checklist we use for PrivateLink tests and a stub for the cert rotation webhook. Once Sofia drops the CIDR I'll create a draft CloudFormation snippet you can drop into a SharedServices stack to reserve the endpoint subnet.

Open questions for your infra team:
- Do you have any additional inbound ACLs (NACLs with stateful rules) that might interfere with the ENI addresses?
- Do you require traffic to be inspected by a corporate firewall appliance (we can proxy through it but it'll add latency and complexity)?

I'll schedule the deep-dive for Thu 16:00 PT; Ben will send the invite.

--
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
[Attachment: kitewave-networking-answers.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)]
